page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance operating on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor with a clock speed of 2.6 GHz, it features 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs via dedicated CPU allocation with hyperthreading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Memory availability is set at 8.0 GB total, yielding a resource ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware specifications show no attached local storage and 0 GPU accelerators. Baseline network connectivity reaches 2 Gbps bandwidth, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned. Instruction set support includes AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 extensions are not supported. Synthetic benchmark evaluation demonstrates average single-core processing with a Geekbench single-core score of 1305.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 23.96 GB/sec. In contrast, multi-threaded CPU performance ranks in lower tiers, yielding a stress-ng multi-core score of 1535.77 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2939.0.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for light compute tasks that require dedicated CPU resources without demanding extensive memory capacity or local disk IOPS. Multi-core performance limitations make it less suitable for high-concurrency or compute-heavy parallel applications. Workload fit includes basic microservices, lightweight web serving, simple API backends, utility scripts, and single-threaded data compression tasks.
description: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, it provides 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading. The instance contains 8.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), 16 MB L3 cache, and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It includes no local disk storage and zero GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its single-core performance in average ranges with a Geekbench single-core score of 1305.0, while multi-threaded results rank in lower tiers, such as a PassMark CPU score of 5590.46 and an uncached memory read speed of 31.36 GB/sec. Given its lean resource configuration and dedicated vCPU allocation, the ecs.c6a.xlarge offers an entry-tier compute option suited for lightweight backend services, basic microservices, single-threaded processing, and utility workloads.
